scenario: Two rule-graph cycles in disjoint SCCs, `one_a`/`one_b` and `two_a`/`two_b`, bridged by one acyclic edge (`one_a` also matches S4, which `two_a` emits), must both be reported: any directed cycle is reported (LCYC.3.3.1), by rule name (LCYC.3.3.2). The expectation is `message_contains: two_a`, which a report naming only the `one_a` cycle does not carry; the error code fires either way. The trap it guards: a search started from `two_a` reaches the `one_a` cycle before its own, and a checker that reports one cycle per search root and skips duplicates drops the second cycle. Every rule emits one schema, so the search order is declaration order, not set iteration.
rules_ds:
schema S1 scope logical:
    kind: String key

schema S2 scope logical:
    kind: String key

schema S3 scope logical:
    kind: String key

schema S4 scope logical:
    kind: String key

rule one_a:
    S1 a where a.kind == "x"
    S4 d where d.kind == "q"
->
    emit S2 logical kind: "y"

rule one_b:
    S2 b where b.kind == "y"
->
    emit S1 logical kind: "x"

rule two_a:
    S3 c where c.kind == "p"
->
    emit S4 logical kind: "q"

rule two_b:
    S4 d where d.kind == "q"
->
    emit S3 logical kind: "p"
